note: Missing `accessToken` — the Management Client's token is the evidence of the person's authority.
Unknown top-level request member — HCP's `GET /v2/rules` takes no parameters (HCP 9.4.14), so there is no filter.
Empty `accessToken` — a token has at least one character.
Missing `rules` — HCP answers 200 with a `rules` array, empty when there is none (HCP 9.4.14).
A cursor in the response — the rules list is not paginated (HCP 9.4.14).
A rule without `ruleId` — the provider sets one on every rule (HCP 6.3).
A rule with neither `operators` nor `requires` — HCP requires one of them, or both (HCP 6.3, 9.4.14).
